clue.text: Full value obtained from Tory showmen

indicators.note: the answer is got out of these words by rearranging their letters, so obtained from signals the anagram

explanation.surface: A party member gets good value out of some entertainers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained from' asks you to rework the letters of TORY SHOWMEN into a new phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting your money's worth means receiving full value for what you paid.

clue.text: Short item of late news

parts.note: the late are the dead, so news of someone recently dead, and the word for it is itself a shortened form

explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not recent: the item is a death notice, and 'Short' points to the clipped form of obituary.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a notice of a death, and the four-letter form is its usual abbreviation.

clue.text: See what a rent the — Casca made" (Julius Caesar, Act 3)

definitions.text: See what a rent the — Casca made" (Julius Caesar, Act 3)

parts.words: See what a rent the — Casca made" (Julius Caesar, Act 3)
parts.note: a quotation from Mark Antony's funeral speech with one word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Antony points to the holes in Caesar's cloak and names the jealous conspirator Casca as the one who made one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony describes Casca as jealous of Caesar, the adjective Shakespeare wrote in that line.

clue.text: Rings up about a painful affliction

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word just before is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rings are round letters O, so two of them make OS
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone telephones about an ailment that hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings up' looks like a telephone call; 'up' is the reversal signal in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore is a raw, tender spot on the body that hurts.

clue.text: Classical example of the short circular letter

definitions.text: Classical example of the short circular letter

parts.words: Classical example of the short circular letter
parts.note: a Greek letter, round in shape, whose name means little or short o

explanation.walkthrough: A 'circular letter' sounds like a mailshot; here it is the round letter of the Greek alphabet, whose name means 'little o', the short vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the Greek alphabet's short o, written as a small circle.

clue.text: The parasite of the moment?

definitions.meaning: a small blood-sucking creature that clings to animals
an instant, as in 'back in a second'

explanation.walkthrough: 'of the moment' suggests something fashionable, but it is just the second definition: an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is both a blood-sucking arachnid and, in British speech, a very short time.

clue.text: Train depot I contrived to alarm

indicators.note: the letters are artificially arranged into a new order, which contrived signals

explanation.surface: Something set up at a railway yard to frighten people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' reorders TRAIN DEPOT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Trepidation is fear or anxiety, a state of alarm.

clue.text: The tree that's less valuable than the golden rod?

definitions.text: The tree that's less valuable than the golden rod?

parts.words: The tree that's less valuable than the golden rod?
parts.note: silver ranks below gold, and goldenrod is a garden plant, so a tree named for the lesser metal

explanation.walkthrough: Goldenrod is a yellow-flowered plant; the tree named after the metal ranked below gold is the white-barked birch.
explanation.definitionFit: A white-barked birch is named after the metal worth less than gold, as goldenrod is named after gold.

clue.text: The converse of the economist?

parts.note: an economist here is one who is economical, so the opposite is a wasteful person

explanation.walkthrough: 'economist' is read as someone thrifty, not a scholar of economics; the opposite is a reckless waster of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift wastes money, the opposite of a careful saver.

clue.text: A load that isn't easy to carry

definitions.text: A load that isn't easy to carry

parts.words: A load that isn't easy to carry
parts.note: a weight that is hard to bear, literally or as a figurative strain

explanation.definitionFit: A weighty load is one that is hard to carry, literally or as a trouble.

clue.text: Latin is seen as this by our modern educationists

definitions.text: Latin is seen as this by our modern educationists

indicators.note: modern educators rework the subject, so their handling rearranges the words before them

explanation.surface: A grumble that today's teachers regard the classical language as unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and LATIN IS SEEN rearranged by the 'modern educationists' gives the word they would apply to Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inessential is not needed, which is how modern teaching treats Latin.

clue.text: Carried away by artillery exercises

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Someone is swept away by gunners' drills.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rapt means being entranced, transported with delight.

clue.text: Eager to join in an Irish lament

definitions.meaning: a wailing song of mourning for the dead in Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to sing along at an Irish wake.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen means enthusiastic, and an Irish keen is a wailing funeral song (from Irish caoine).

clue.text: Men I put to rout in a planta ti on of conifers

indicators.note: routing an army scatters it, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Soldiers are scattered through a forest plantation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rout' scatters MEN I PUT. The clue's 'planta ti on' is the printed word plantation broken by spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinetum is an arboretum devoted to pines and other conifers.

clue.text: Goes on board to play

definitions.meaning: goes as a plural noun are turns, as in 'whose go is it?'
what players make on a chess or draughts board

explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' reads as a verb but is the plural noun meaning turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Moves are players' turns, and also the steps made with pieces on a game board.

clue.text: It turns in 14 reasons for action, possibly

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the answer to 14 down, which is MOVES

indicators.note: turns means the short word beside it is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something rotates inside a numbered clue's answer to explain behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The bare number '14' stands for the answer to that clue; 'turns' and 'in' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Motives are the reasons that drive someone to act.

clue.text: Clear the field of opponents?

parts.note: in battle, the last stage of wiping out remaining enemy forces

explanation.walkthrough: 'field' is a battlefield, where the final clean-up removes the last of the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to finish off remaining resistance, cleaning up after the main fight.

clue.text: Fifty ducks turning on a wise old Greek

indicators.note: turning means the piece beside it is reversed

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O, so ducks are OS
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flock of waterfowl spins round an ancient sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes SO from OS; then L and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was the Athenian lawgiver, one of the Seven Sages of Greece.

clue.text: A tax office, maybe

definitions.meaning: a levy charged on goods, such as customs or excise
an obligation or job one must do, as in 'the office of host'

explanation.surface: A tax office, the building where revenue is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, a tax office; split it into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty is both a levy on goods and a task one is obliged to perform, an office.

clue.text: Skilful apprentice in Lincoln

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's short name
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A skilled trainee working in the Lincolnshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is the US president, not the English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means competent, having skill.

clue.text: Established a good position at Wimbledon?

definitions.meaning: in tennis, being one set ahead of the opponent

explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship, where a player leading by one set is 'a set up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up is to establish, and a tennis player a set up leads the match by one set.

clue.text: Bowlines?

parts.note: split as bow lines, the cords on a bow, rather than the sailor's knot

explanation.walkthrough: A bowline is a sailor's knot; read it as 'bow lines', the cords stretched on an archer's or violinist's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Strings are the cords of a bow, so they are its lines.

clue.text: What unlicensed broadcasters are charged for front-page publicity?

definitions.text: What unlicensed broadcasters are charged for front-page publicity?

parts.words: What unlicensed broadcasters are charged for front-page publicity?
parts.note: radio stations broadcasting without a licence get a name, and the headline rates of a paper are a pun on fees charged

explanation.walkthrough: Unlicensed radio stations go by the name of seafaring raiders; 'charged' plays on the prices of the front page and on being accused of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal radio broadcasters are called pirate stations, and newspaper front pages carry the top rates.

clue.text: Frenzied satyr describing New Testament despots

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the first piece encloses the second
frenzied means wildly agitated, so the letters of the word beside it are thrown about

explanation.surface: A wild woodland god draws scenes of Gospel tyrants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round something, so the jumbled word encloses the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Despots are absolute rulers, often cruel ones.

clue.text: White-faced buffoon I do wrong to shoot out

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the shooting word goes round the rest

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game, as in a pot shot
taken as written
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A clown confesses to being wrong to fire at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot out' reads as a gunfight, but 'out' only says the shooting word lies outside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad clown of French pantomime, with a whitened face and loose white costume.

clue.text: A Welsh admirer of fame? Not me!

indicators.note: not me means this word is to be left out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Welsh fan of celebrity is them, and denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ME from OF FAME. Offa was the Mercian king who built the dyke against the Welsh, so calling him a Welsh admirer is meant ironically, as the question mark shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mercian king raised a long earthwork to keep the Welsh out, the reverse of an admirer.

clue.text: The craft Jason mastered

parts.note: craft as a vessel and mastered as commanded, not a skill learned

explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' sounds like a skill and 'mastered' like learning it; read them as a ship and its commander, the Greek hero who sought the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship that carried Jason and the Argonauts.

clue.text: Decidedly close victory at cards?

definitions.meaning: to shut something forcefully, as a door
winning every trick in bridge or whist

explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like an adjective (a narrow win) but is the verb to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Slam means to shut with force, and a grand slam takes all the tricks at bridge.

clue.text: High table?

parts.note: not the top table at a college dinner but a raised flat landform

explanation.walkthrough: High table is where dons dine at a British college; here it is tableland, a raised plateau, from the Spanish word for table.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a flat-topped hill, and the word is Spanish for table.

clue.text: Extra soldiers brought into the Middle East

indicators.note: brought into means the soldiers are placed inside the region

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the Middle East
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Extra troops are deployed to the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought into' reads as troops deployed; it signals one abbreviation placed inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: More means additional, further.

clue.text: U.N. version of speech made by Stalin on art

indicators.note: made here means fashioned from, so the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A UN rendering of a Soviet leader's lecture about art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' reworks STALIN ON ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A translation renders speech in another language, as UN interpreters do.

clue.text: He'll let us know when health-giving drinks should be taken

definitions.text: He'll let us know when health-giving drinks should be taken

parts.words: He'll let us know when health-giving drinks should be taken
parts.note: drinks to someone's health are toasts at a banquet, announced by the person running proceedings

explanation.walkthrough: 'health-giving drinks' are not tonics but toasts drunk to someone's health at a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The master of ceremonies at a banquet announces the toasts and the speakers.
